blueprint_topic: Management of Care — early multidisciplinary discharge planning, community referrals, follow-up, and post-discharge coordination after complex traumatic injury
stem: A client recovering from complex traumatic injuries will need outpatient rehabilitation and social-care support after hospital discharge. Which case-management action best supports continuity of care?

options.A: Start multidisciplinary discharge planning early, document follow-up and referrals, and agree on a key contact for ongoing coordination after discharge.
options.B: Finalize inpatient rehabilitation goals before involving community teams, then send referrals once the discharge date is fixed so outpatient teams can make their own plan.
options.C: Transfer the hospital rehabilitation summary at discharge and let community services decide the follow-up schedule and primary contact after the first visit.
options.D: Secure equipment and coverage arrangements first, then address community rehabilitation referrals and ongoing contact after the client returns home.

rationale: A is correct. Current NICE guideline NG211 recommends early multidisciplinary discharge planning, reassessment of rehabilitation needs before discharge, a coordinated and integrated approach through transfer to outpatient and community rehabilitation, documentation of how rehabilitation will continue including referrals and review appointments, and agreement on a key contact after discharge when ongoing rehabilitation and health or social-care support are needed. NCSBN places referrals, continuity, multidisciplinary collaboration, discharge planning, and resource coordination within Management of Care. B is incorrect because community practitioners and referrals should be engaged before discharge rather than after inpatient goals are finalized in isolation. C is incomplete because continuity planning should establish follow-up and contact arrangements before the client is simply handed off to community services. D is incorrect because equipment or coverage tasks may be important, but they should not postpone community rehabilitation referrals and contact planning until after the client returns home.
educational_objective: Use case management to begin multidisciplinary discharge planning early, coordinate community referrals and follow-up, and establish ongoing contact arrangements before a client with complex rehabilitation needs leaves the hospital.
source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Rehabilitation after traumatic injury (NG211) — Recommendations; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: NICE NG211 published 2022-01-18 and current recommendations rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: NICE NG211 current Recommendations, section 1.8: 1.8.1 recommends early multidisciplinary discharge planning for smooth transition to outpatient/community services; 1.8.2 requires reassessment of needs and review of the rehabilitation plan before discharge; 1.8.14 recommends coordinated, consistent and integrated multidisciplinary support through transfer; 1.8.15 requires the rehabilitation plan/handover to document ongoing support, follow-up, community rehabilitation, referrals and review appointments; 1.8.16 recommends pre-discharge planning with community practitioners for significant ongoing needs; 1.8.21 provides a single point of hospital contact for a limited transition period; 1.8.22 requires inpatient and community teams to agree the key contact after discharge when ongoing rehabilitation and health/social-care support are needed. NICE rationale states a single point of contact reduces communication delays/duplication and supports access to outpatient/community rehabilitation. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care supports referrals, discharge/continuity planning, multidisciplinary collaboration, plan-of-care coordination, and resource use.
source_claim_supported: Current NICE guidance directly supports early coordinated discharge planning, pre-discharge community involvement, documented follow-up/referrals, and defined post-discharge contact for people with ongoing complex rehabilitation needs. NCSBN supports the nursing case-management and continuity construct. The stem uses complex traumatic injury rather than a TBI-specific rehabilitation claim to remain within the directly supported scope of NG211.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify/collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess need for referrals, safely discharge clients, initiate/evaluate/update the plan of care, and utilize resources to promote continuity and quality care.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7 / PDF pageno 10 was freshly screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation on 2026-08-20. NICE clinical claims use current HTML. No NICE PDF evidence is relied on for this item.
correction_summary: Original Q1974 used a traumatic-brain-injury-specific stem despite NG211 not covering specific TBI rehabilitation interventions, and the correct answer was substantially longer than distractors. The item was rebuilt around the directly supported broader population of complex traumatic injury. All four options now describe realistic discharge/case-management sequences, while the key integrates early planning, pre-discharge referrals/follow-up, and agreed ongoing contact without importing UK-specific administrative infrastructure. Independent post-fetch reread found no unresolved source, scope, portability, continuity, ambiguity, cueing, blueprint, or second-answer conflict.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates early multidisciplinary planning, documented referrals/follow-up, and an agreed post-discharge contact before the transition.
option_audit.B: Plausible inpatient-first sequencing error; incorrect because current guidance supports early community coordination rather than waiting until inpatient goals and a fixed discharge date are complete.
option_audit.C: Plausible handover-focused approach; incomplete because follow-up and key-contact arrangements should be planned as part of the transition rather than left until after the first community visit.
option_audit.D: Plausible administrative/resource priority; incorrect because equipment and coverage work should not defer rehabilitation referrals and continuity arrangements until after discharge.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 152, B 171, C 157, D 148 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and choices are substantially balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are realistic case-management/discharge workflows and differ mainly in timing and continuity rather than obvious safety language.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: Independent adversarial reread found no defensible second answer. B delays community coordination, C leaves follow-up/contact undefined until after transfer, and D postpones referrals/contact until after home arrival; A is uniquely aligned with current guidance.
